description: 1043 - Data Engineer (Neo4j/Cypher/Knowledge Graphs) · Semi-Senior · Remoto · Argentina Ubicación: Argentina Modalidad: 100% remoto Tipo de contratación: Relación de dependencia (full-time) Industria / Proyecto: LegalTech / Inteligencia Legal y Regulatoria con IA Zona horaria: Argentina (ART / UTC-3) Seniority: Semi-Senior (3 a 5 años de experiencia) Conocé Darwoft En Darwoft desarrollamos software que genera impacto real. Somos una compañía tecnológica latinoamericana que trabaja junto a empresas de diferentes partes del mundo, creando soluciones digitales innovadoras, escalables y de alto valor. Nuestra cultura combina excelencia técnica, colaboración, aprendizaje continuo y una fuerte orientación a las personas. La Inteligencia Artificial forma parte de nuestra manera de trabajar, innovar y resolver problemas. Buscamos incorporar nuevas tecnologías para construir mejores productos y potenciar las capacidades de nuestros equipos. Si te apasiona la tecnología, disfrutás resolver desafíos complejos y querés participar en proyectos donde tu trabajo tenga impacto, nos encantaría conocerte. Sobre el rol Estamos buscando un/a Data Engineer Semi-Senior con experiencia práctica en Neo4j, Cypher y modelado de datos en grafos para sumarse a un proyecto innovador de LegalTech enfocado en transformar la manera en que se organiza, conecta y consulta información legal, tributaria, contable y regulatoria. Vas a participar en el desarrollo y evolución de un Knowledge Graph que permitirá relacionar grandes volúmenes de información, identificar conexiones semánticas y potenciar soluciones de búsqueda inteligente basadas en Inteligencia Artificial. Esta posición combina Data Engineering, Graph Databases e Inteligencia Artificial, con un fuerte enfoque en la construcción de soluciones productivas, escalables y mantenibles. Trabajarás junto a equipos de Data Science, Backend e IA para transformar modelos conceptuales, taxonomías y ontologías en estructuras de grafos eficientes que alimenten arquitecturas de recuperación de información como RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation). Buscamos una persona con una base sólida en ingeniería de datos, experiencia real trabajando con Neo4j y motivación por seguir desarrollándose en Knowledge Graphs, búsqueda semántica y GraphRAG. ¿Qué vas a hacer? Modelado de grafos: Diseñar, implementar y mantener modelos de datos en Neo4j, representando entidades, relaciones, jerarquías y estructuras complejas de información. Ingeniería de datos: Construir y optimizar pipelines ETL/ELT para ingesta, transformación, validación y actualización de datos estructurados y no estructurados. Desarrollo con Cypher: Crear y optimizar consultas complejas para recuperación de información, navegación de relaciones y procesamiento de datos en grafos. Implementación de Knowledge Graphs: Transformar taxonomías, ontologías y modelos conceptuales definidos por Data Science en estructuras productivas dentro de Neo4j. Integración con IA y RAG: Participar en la integración de Neo4j con embeddings, búsqueda vectorial y arquitecturas de recuperación semántica. Optimización de performance: Mejorar consultas, estrategias de indexación, consistencia de datos y escalabilidad de la base de grafos. Integración con Backend: Desarrollar integraciones mediante Python o Node.js para conectar los datos del grafo con aplicaciones, APIs y servicios internos. Calidad de datos: Implementar validaciones, controles automatizados y buenas prácticas para garantizar la integridad y confiabilidad de la información. Trabajo interdisciplinario: Colaborar con especialistas en Data Science, Inteligencia Artificial y desarrollo de software para evolucionar la arquitectura de datos. ¿Qué buscamos? Experiencia: Entre 3 y 5 años de experiencia profesional en Data Engineering, Data Platform Engineering o posiciones similares. Neo4j: Experiencia práctica diseñando, implementando y manteniendo soluciones basadas en bases de datos de grafos. Cypher: Buen dominio del lenguaje para desarrollar consultas complejas, recorrer relaciones y optimizar operaciones sobre grafos. Modelado de datos: Conocimiento de modelos Property Graph, nodos, relaciones, labels, propiedades y buenas prácticas de diseño. ETL/ELT: Experiencia desarrollando pipelines de ingesta, transformación e integración de datos. Programación: Manejo de Python o Node.js para procesamiento de datos, automatización o integración con servicios. Optimización: Conocimiento de índices, constraints, optimización de consultas y performance de bases de datos. Arquitectura de datos: Capacidad para transformar requerimientos funcionales y técnicos en modelos de datos escalables y mantenibles. data-dense interfaces with a focus on clarity Ability to rapidly gain an understanding of a technical domain and associated customer needs and user workflows in order to design effective experiences description: Signicatis a pan-European digital identity company that makes it easy and safe for organisations to know who they are interacting with online. Using our proprietary technology, we help companies and public organisations securely verify the identities of people and businesses, authenticate users, and enable compliant electronic document signing, so their customers can access services and complete online processes with confidence. Today, Signicat employs over 530 people across 20 offices in 15 European countries. We work with leading banks, fintechs, telcos, public authorities, healthcare providers, and enterprises across retail and mobility to deliver trusted digital identity and onboarding solutions at scale. Joining Signicat means contributing to a mission that has a real impact on how society works and trusting each other in an increasingly digital world. About the Role Imagine a software development environment where AI agents can collaborate, plan complex tasks, write code, run tests, and help engineers turn ideas into working software. That's what we're building. As a Platform Engineer in Signicat's AI Foundations team, you'll help design and build our internal AI Software Factory: a platform that enables teams of autonomous AI agents to work together, interact securely with our systems, and accelerate how we build software. This isn't just about integrating LLM APIs. We're building the foundations for agent-driven software engineering, tackling challenges around orchestration, distributed execution, state management, sandboxing, security, and human-agent collaboration. Our platform runs on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and Kubernetes, with Go as our primary programming language. You'll join a team exploring the boundaries of what's possible with AI agents, combining experimentation with solid software engineering principles to turn ambitious ideas into reliable, production-ready systems. How You'll Make An Impact Build the AI Software Factory: Design and develop the core services, APIs, and infrastructure that enable AI agents to plan, execute, and collaborate on complex software engineering tasks. Orchestrate intelligent agents: Build systems that coordinate multiple specialized agents, manage dependencies, schedule work, and support long-running, asynchronous workflows. Design reliable agent runtimes: Develop secure, stateful execution environments that manage agent lifecycles, context, tool invocations, retries, recovery, and execution isolation. Make autonomous execution safe: Implement sandboxing, fine-grained permissions, and security boundaries that allow agents to interact with code, tools, and internal systems without compromising security. Connect agents to the real world: Integrate LLMs, development workflows, internal APIs, and external tools through secure, extensible interfaces and emerging standards such as MCP and A2A. Enable human-agent collaboration: Help create systems where engineers can guide, supervise, and collaborate with autonomous agents, maintaining control over important decisions. Shape the future of AI engineering: Evaluate emerging technologies, challenge existing approaches, experiment with new architectural patterns, and help define how autonomous software engineering evolves at Signicat. Solve interesting engineering problems: Apply your understanding of distributed systems, concurrency, fault tolerance, and software architecture to challenges that don't always have established solutions. Why We'll Love You You have strong software engineering experience, ideally with Go, and enjoy building robust backend services, APIs, and distributed systems. You're comfortable working with Kubernetes, containers, and cloud-native infrastructure, ideally on Google Cloud Platform. You think beyond individual services and understand how to design systems that handle concurrency, failures, asynchronous execution, and complex state transitions. You care about clean architecture, well-designed APIs, maintainable code, and automated testing. You understand the importance of security, particularly around authentication, authorization, isolation, and executing untrusted workloads. You're curious about LLMs and autonomous agents, including concepts such as tool calling, context management, multi-agent collaboration, and agent orchestration. You enjoy exploring emerging technologies, experimenting with new approaches, and turning promising ideas into practical solutions. You're comfortable navigating ambiguity, taking ownership of challenging technical problems, and helping shape architectural decisions. You enjoy sharing knowledge, collaborating with others, and challenging assumptions to find better solutions. Bonus Points You've built systems using agent frameworks such as Google ADK, or worked with protocols like MCP or A2A. You have experience with sandboxing or workload isolation technologies such as gVisor, WebAssembly, or container-based execution environments. You've worked with event-driven architectures, workflow engines, distributed schedulers, or systems supporting long-running processes. You've experimented with AI coding agents, autonomous development workflows, or multi-agent systems. You have experience designing secure integrations with external services, including OAuth and delegated authorization. You've explored graph-based architectures, RDF, SPARQL, or event-driven systems, and are excited about using these concepts to model complex relationships, agent workflows, and dynamic, reactive applications. This is a wish list, not a checklist. You don't need to have worked with every technology or built AI agents before. If you're a strong engineer who loves solving complex problems and is excited about shaping the future of AI-driven software development, we'd love to hear from you. What we offer: Tailored benefits package by location - we aim to empower our employees by offering customised benefits suited to each market Your tech, your way - choose the tech gear that aligns with your comfort and meets your preferences Remote work style -while you embrace a remote environment, we support occasional in-person gatherings to strengthen the teamwork Work-life balance - enjoy an extra 5 paid days off annually, and we make sure to celebrate your work anniversaries to acknowledge the milestones you achieve Health & Wellness - we prioritise your physical and mental well-being by providing designated packs and access to the Headspace app Continuous growth - quarterly development talks, a dedicated time during working hours each week for training and development, access to Udemy courses, defined career paths, and internal mentorship opportunities Customised onboarding - we will prepare an Onboarding Plan to ensure an easy and smooth beginning Be part of an international team - the opportunity to work from any other Signicat office for 2 months per year and 3 weeks per year from any EU country Empowering feedback culture - by using employee engagement tools, we ensure that every voice is heard, empowering us to grow together Meet-ups - frequent office gatherings and biennial Kick-off event to bring every Signicat under one roof that you don’t want to miss Salary: €70,000-€90,000 gross yearly. We are open to discussing the salary based on your skills and competencies. Originally posted on Himalayas

description: Who We Are At RelationalAI, we’re solving one of the most important challenges in artificial intelligence: how to teach large language models the logic, semantics, and business context of the modern enterprise. Frontier models are trained almost entirely on public data — they can speak about the world, but they don’t understand your business. We fix that. RelationalAI has pioneered a breakthrough called Superalignment — technology that enables LLMs to learn natively from private, structured enterprise data inside the data cloud. By combining this with relational knowledge graphs and our proprietary neuro/symbolic-relational reasoners, we deliver trustworthy decision intelligence: systems that use semantic models to truly understand how a business operates and can reason across its data to drive better outcomes. We’re a globally distributed team of engineers, scientists, and builders redefining how AI learns from data. We believe that high-stakes decisions deserve frontier intelligence — intelligence that’s explainable, aligned, and grounded in reality. If you’re driven by curiosity, thrive in complexity, and want to help build the system that brings true understanding to enterprise AI, you’ll feel right at home here. The Role You will be embedded inside our customers' hardest problems, and you will own the outcome until it works in production. You'll sit with executives, domain experts, and data teams to find the decisions that actually move their business - inventory that's in the wrong place, risk concentrations nobody can see, fraud patterns that only emerge across three systems, capacity plans built on guesses. Then you'll model their world in our ontology, formulate the reasoning problem, write the PyRel, and ship something that runs against their real data in their own Snowflake account. Every engagement here produces two deliverables. The first is the one the customer sees: a working decision system that changes how they operate. The second is the one that matters most to us: the pile of things you had to invent because our platform didn't have them yet. The modelling pattern you hand-rolled. The constraint formulation that should have been a primitive. The three-hour workaround where an API should have existed. You bring those back, you argue for them, and the strongest of them become product. That second deliverable is why this role exists. If you only ever deliver the first one, we've hired a consultant. We're not hiring consultants. You'll operate with unusual autonomy: you decide what's worth building, when a workaround is acceptable and when it's technical debt we'll regret, and when to tell a customer their real problem is not the one they asked about. You'll be technical enough that when something breaks in a customer environment, you find the root cause yourself rather than filing a ticket and waiting. What You'll Do Own outcomes end to end - discovery, modelling, implementation, performance tuning, production hardening, and the measurement that proves it worked. Not a handoff at each stage. Yours. Build, not describe - design and ship decision solutions on our modelling, reasoning, and learning stack: ontologies over customer data, rules, graph analytics, optimisation formulations, predictive models Fill the gaps yourself - when a customer workflow is blocked on something the platform doesn't do, scope it and build it. Then push the general version upstream: read our source, form a hypothesis before you escalate, open the PR. Close the loop with Product - every deployment generates a signal. Bring back reproductions, patterns, and specific failure modes ("the only way I could express this was by abusing X in this way"), not vibes. You are one of the loudest inputs into our roadmap. Run technical discovery that gets to the truth - workshops, demos, and proofs of concept designed to find out whether we can actually solve the problem, not to look impressive. Leave things better than you found them - document as you go, in the repo, same week. Turn one-off work into reusable reference implementations so the next person starts where you finished. No branch of yours should be diverging for a month. Refuse shortcuts that compound - no undocumented config drift, no "it works now" without knowing why it broke, no restarting the service before you've captured the evidence. Who You Are You thrive in ambiguity and move with intent. You're motivated by deep understanding and meaningful impact. Owner, not participant. You take full accountability for the outcome, not your slice of it. When something is broken and it's nobody's job, it becomes yours. You build. Your instinct in the face of a hard problem is to open an editor, not a deck. You'd rather show a working prototype on real data than a diagram of one. High conviction, low ego. You argue hard for what you believe, you're direct about what's wrong, and you change your mind quickly when the evidence turns. You challenge ideas without making it personal - people leave arguments with you feeling sharper, not smaller. Rigorous. You root-cause things. You can explain both why it broke and why your fix works. Surface symptoms don't satisfy you. Fast in unfamiliar territory. Dropped into a codebase, a domain, or a data model you've never seen, you're useful within days. "I only do backend" and "that's not my job" are phrases you don't use. High tolerance for friction. Enterprise environments are messy - broken data, VDI access, security reviews, politics. You route around it and keep shipping. Impact-driven. You want the thing you built to still be running, and still be load-bearing, two years from now. What This Role Is Not We'd rather be blunt than waste your time: It is not demo-and-handoff pre-sales. You don't disappear after the POC; you're there when it goes to production. It is not staff augmentation. You own outcomes, not hours or ticket queues. It is not advisory. We deliver working software, not recommendations. It is not a support role. You deploy new things; you don't maintain someone else's legacy. Qualifications 5+ years building and shipping production software, at least some of it inside customer or partner environments Demonstrated end-to-end ownership: you have personally taken something from an ambiguous problem statement to running in production, and you can walk us through the whole arc, including what went wrong Strong SQL and deep familiarity with cloud data platforms (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift) Strong programming ability - Python primarily; comfort with declarative or logic-style languages is a real advantage Comfortable reading unfamiliar source code, interpreting stack traces, and debugging systems you didn't write Able to hold your own with both a VP of Supply Chain and a staff data engineer, in the same meeting Comfortable operating in high-autonomy, high-velocity, low-instruction environments Preferred Qualifications Built analytical, decision, or reasoning applications that reached production and stayed there Experience with optimization, constraint solving, rule engines, graph algorithms, or ML on structured data Semantic modelling, data pipelines, and governance in real enterprise settings Track record of upstream contribution - features, tools, or abstractions you built for one customer that became standard for everyone Prior experience in enterprise technology, AI, or analytics platforms How We Hire Our loop is designed to test the job, not trivia. Expect a technical screen; a session where you navigate and extend a system you've never seen before; a problem-decomposition session on a realistic customer scenario; and a conversation about ownership with the hiring manager. We're looking for how you think when you don't know the answer. The Solution Engineer position offers a base salary range of $170,000 to $200,000, along with equity and comprehensive benefits. Please note that this range serves as a guideline; actual total compensation may vary based on factors such as experience, skill set, qualifications, and geographic location. Why RelationalAI At RelationalAI, you will: Work from anywhere in the world Earn competitive salary + equity Enjoy open PTO, flexible schedules, and recharge weeks Access global benefits, mental-health support, and learning stipends Join a transparent, inclusive, and globally connected culture that values curiosity, excellence, and impact Regular team offsites and global events – Building strong connections while working remotely through team offsites and global events that bring everyone together. A culture of transparency & knowledge-sharing – Open communication through team standups, fireside chats, and open meetings. Country Hiring Guidelines: RelationalAI hires people from around the world. All of our roles are remote; however, some locations might carry specific eligibility requirements. Because of this, understanding location & visa support helps us better prepare to onboard our colleagues. Our People Operations team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruitment process. How to Apply If you’re driven by understanding, powered by curiosity, and ready to help shape the next era of enterprise intelligence — we’d love to hear from you. Join us and help build the reasoning layer for the modern enterprise. Privacy Policy: EU residents applying for positions at RelationalAI can see our Privacy Policy here. California residents applying for positions at RelationalAI can see our Privacy Policy here RelationalAI is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, race, religion, pregnancy, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations and ordinances.

title: Solution Engineer

description: Alimentiv is a global CRO with a singular focus: advancing therapies for patients with gastrointestinal diseases. GI is our WHY and for more than 30 years that purpose has driven our scientific rigour, operational excellence, and deep therapeutic expertise, including supporting more than 70% of IBD compounds in development. We operate as a private, profit-with-purpose company, channeling our commercial success back into scientific research, technology, and our people. With approximately 700 people across multiple countries and three service lines, we are growing deliberately, and the capability of our leaders and our organization is central to how we get there. If you want to do meaningful work, build something real, and invest back in research that changes lives — we want to meet you! Job Overview As a Senior Clinical Research Associate, you will play a key role in the successful delivery of clinical trials by independently managing clinical site monitoring and site management activities across Portugal and Spain, from study start-up through close-out. You will act as a primary point of contact for investigative sites in these countries, ensuring compliance with protocols, ICH-GCP, applicable regulations and study requirements while supporting high-quality patient data and study delivery. This is a senior individual contributor role with responsibility for supporting site performance, resolving issues, maintaining study documentation and providing guidance and mentorship to junior CRAs. You will work closely with Clinical Operations, Project Management, sponsors and other cross-functional teams in a dynamic clinical research environment. Key Responsibilities: Independently conduct and document onsite and remote monitoring activities, including site qualification, initiation, monitoring and close-out visits across Portugal and Spain. Ensure investigative sites comply with study protocols, ICH-GCP, applicable regulations, SOPs and project-specific requirements. Serve as a primary point of contact for assigned sites, managing site-related questions, issues, action items and protocol deviations through to resolution. Review clinical trial data, source documentation and study systems to ensure accuracy, completeness, data integrity and compliance. Support site selection, activation and recruitment activities, working with sites to achieve study milestones and patient recruitment targets. Ensure sites are appropriately trained on protocols, study systems, processes and applicable requirements throughout the study lifecycle. Maintain oversight of essential study documentation, including ISF and TMF, ensuring documents are complete, accurate and filed in a timely manner. Collaborate with sponsors, project teams, vendors and investigative sites to support study timelines, resolve issues and maintain effective working relationships. Participate in audits and inspections, Investigator Meetings, study meetings and other project activities as required. Provide mentoring and support to CRA I and II colleagues, participate in co-monitoring and CRA assessment activities, and contribute to process improvement initiatives. Skills & Qualifications Bachelor’s degree (Honours) in Life Sciences, Health Sciences, Pharmacy, Nursing or a related discipline; a Master’s degree is preferred. 4–6 years of relevant clinical research experience, with 7–9 years preferred. Strong clinical site monitoring experience across clinical trial activities from site start-up through close-out. Thorough knowledge of ICH-GCP, clinical research principles and applicable local regulatory requirements. Experience with Phase I–IV clinical trials preferred. Proficiency with clinical trial systems such as EDC, IRT, eTMF, CTMS and Microsoft Office, with experience in systems such as Medidata Rave or Oracle InForm preferred. Strong understanding of site management, including site activation, recruitment, training, issue resolution and maintenance of essential documentation. Excellent communication, interpersonal and relationship-management skills, with the ability to work effectively with investigative sites, sponsors and cross-functional teams. Strong organisational, problem-solving and prioritisation skills, with a high level of attention to detail and a sense of urgency. Ability to work independently, demonstrate sound judgement and manage competing priorities in a results-driven environment. Experience mentoring or supporting junior CRAs is preferred. Willingness and ability to travel approximately 40–60%, depending on project requirements and geographic location. Valid driver’s licence required. Fluent written and verbal English and Spanish What We Offer In addition, as an Alimentiv Employee, you’re also eligible for the following programs: Education Reimbursement program for full-time employees Monthly Cell Phone and Remote Work Allowance (dependent on role eligibility) One time office setup allowance (can be used to purchase a scanner/printer, extra monitor, office furniture, etc.) Working while visiting program – up to 4 weeks per year! Flexible Summer Hours Program from May – September Employee referral incentive – we know great people know other great people, and we think that warrants recognition! Full-time employees also become beneficiaries of the Alimentiv Trust after one year of employment, and permanent members after 5 years of employment Optional formal mentorship program (Alimentorship); country/region annual social events in person; leadership development programs for people leaders in accordance with your seniority; social committee and several other optional initiatives designed to support you in feeling like part of the Alimentiv team! Additional benefits may be available depending on the country of employment and are subject to local policies and eligibility. Our Services End-to-end GI clinical trial services, from protocol design through submission support Central medical imaging management and endoscopic reading Precision medicine and biomarker solutions Real-world evidence and clinical consulting Histopathology and lab services through AcelaBio How to Apply To apply for this position, please submit your resume through the Alimentiv Careers Portal or via LinkedIn’s Easy Apply. Resumes must be submitted in English. Equal Opportunity and Accessibility Alimentiv is committed to building a diverse, inclusive and respectful workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer and consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, colour, ethnicity, national origin, religion or belief, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital or family status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Accommodations are available upon request for persons with disabilities throughout the recruitment and selection process. Requests can be directed to recruitment@alimentiv.com. Compensation Additional Information Stay Alert to Recruitment Scams Alimentiv is aware of a continued increase in phishing scams, which use various methods of attack via email, text, voice and social media, including individuals posing as our recruiters and contacting candidates with fraudulent opportunities. Our hiring process always includes direct engagement with a recruiter or hiring manager, and we will never ask for sensitive personal information early in the process. Official communication will only come from company email addresses containing "@alimentiv.com". If you are contacted about an open job at Alimentiv, please verify the domain of the sender's email address and confirm that you are being asked to apply on this website. If something doesn't feel right, we encourage you to verify before responding. If you believe you have been the victim of a phishing scam, please contact your local government cyber authority to report it.

description: Product Marketing Lead In Brief We're a rapidly growing startup on a mission to make healthcare proactive by empowering physicians, nurses, and care team members with real-time data to save lives. As our Product Marketing Lead, you will own how we show up for health system leaders. That covers the sales content that moves deals forward, the messaging behind each new module, and the story we tell customers who are ready to grow with us. Who We Are Bayesian Health's mission is to improve patient outcomes by empowering clinicians with the insights they need to make the right decision for the right patient at the point of care. We're a diverse team of clinicians, engineers, AI experts, product designers, and performance improvement leaders committed to enabling smarter, patient-specific care delivery through unlocking the power of data. We're funded by top tier tech and biotech investors: Obvious Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, American Medical Association's venture arm, Catalio Partners, and LifeForce Capital. Recent recognitions include Forbes AI Top 50, World Economic Forum Tech Pioneer, Time Best Inventions, and BioTech AI Company of the Year. Read more about our peer-reviewed research in Nature Medicine associating our products with improved patient outcomes. About the Role This role spans three connected areas of product marketing: sales enablement, module marketing, and customer expansion. You will own all three end to end. Most of your energy will go to enablement, expansion, and module marketing, in that order of urgency as the field and our roadmap demand. Product marketing is a function we are still building. You will be our dedicated product marketer, so you will set the standards, templates, and systems as much as you follow them. You will decide what gets built next based on what Sales and Client Success tell you is moving deals and renewals. As the team grows, you may have the chance to mentor more junior marketers. What You'll Own Sales Enablement Own the core sales content library, including the sales deck, two-pagers, white papers, and collateral that quantify our impact for buyers and customers. Keep it accurate and current as the product and the market change. Work with Sales to learn which pieces move deals forward and which ones don't. Deal-Specific Content Build tailored content for late-stage opportunities, such as custom one-pagers and slides. Take a rough brief from a sales rep and return a polished deliverable without a heavy process around you. Be able to point to specific content you built that helped advance or close a deal. Competitive Intelligence Maintain competitive intel and battlecards as the market shifts. Keep them current without being asked, so reps never walk into a conversation with outdated information. Product and Module Marketing Develop positioning and messaging by module and buyer. Build module deep-dive materials and lead go-to-market for module launches, including palliative care and deterioration. Customer Expansion Partner with Client Success on expansion messaging, executive steering committee and QBR materials, and release communications for existing customers. Help customers see the value they are already getting and what more is possible. Buyer Messaging Write for the full health system buying committee, including CMOs, CMIOs, CIOs, CFOs, and quality leaders. Translate clinical outcomes and technical capabilities into language that resonates with clinical, operational, and financial stakeholders. Make a business case land with a C-suite, not just a product pitch. Cross-Functional Partnership Join deal calls and QBRs. Pull roadmap details from Product proactively, and work with Clinical to keep every claim credible. Surface what is working in the field and feed market and competitive insight back into the business. What You'll Bring 5+ years of product marketing experience in healthcare technology, with direct experience marketing to health system executive buyers A bachelor's degree A record of building positioning, messaging, enablement, and launch programs that sales teams actually use A track record of deal-specific content tied to advanced or closed opportunities Experience writing for CMOs, CMIOs, CIOs, CFOs, and quality leaders, and supporting long, multi-stakeholder deals into health systems Working knowledge of how enterprise health system deals move, including committee-based buying, clinical validation, IT and security review, and budget cycles Exceptional writing that is clear, credible, and evidence-based, with first drafts that need little rework Self-direction in a fast-moving startup, including the instinct to spot what is missing and build it without being asked Strong partnership habits with Sales, Product, Client Success, and Clinical teams Nice to Haves Product or customer marketing experience with an installed base, including expansion or upsell campaigns Familiarity with clinical AI, clinical decision support, or quality and safety improvement Experience informally mentoring a more junior marketer Life at Bayesian We're a small, mission-driven team building AI tools that help clinicians catch life-threatening conditions earlier. We work remotely but stay closely connected in real time. We believe that closer collaboration helps us move faster for the hospitals and patients who depend on us. Our values guide how we work every day: Patients at the center. We hold ourselves to a high bar for excellence and impact. Hard problems, real breakthroughs. description: Clinical Quality Consultant In Brief We're a rapidly growing startup on a mission to make healthcare proactive by empowering physicians, nurses, and care team members with real-time data to save lives. You'll support product quality for an FDA-cleared, AI-driven clinical platform, from complaint investigation once it's live in hospitals, to the quality system and regulatory record that hold it all together. Who We Are Bayesian Health's mission is to improve patient outcomes by empowering clinicians with the insights they need to make the right decision for the right patient at the point of care. We're a diverse team of clinicians, engineers, AI experts, product designers, and performance improvement leaders committed to enabling smarter, patient-specific care delivery through unlocking the power of data. We're funded by top tier tech and biotech investors: Obvious Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, American Medical Association's venture arm, Catalio Partners, and LifeForce Capital. Recent recognitions include Forbes AI Top 50, World Economic Forum Tech Pioneer, Time Best Inventions, and BioTech AI Company of the Year. Read more about our peer-reviewed research in Nature Medicine associating our products with improved patient outcomes. About the Role When a care team asks why an alert did or did not fire, that question comes to our Clinical Production Support team, and answering it well takes real clinical judgment. Clinical case reviews are the largest share of that work and the heart of this role. You will investigate what happened in a given encounter, reach a sound and defensible conclusion, and communicate it clearly to the clinicians and client teams who asked. Strong clinical reasoning is the foundation. On top of it, you will build a working understanding of how the product behaves, including how flags are generated, how suppression logic works, and how data moves from the EHR into the model. That technical fluency is taught here rather than expected at hire. The same is true of the medical device regulatory side, where you will grow into product complaint handling and, once trained, contribute to the disposition of possible anomalies that gate our releases. This is a function still being built. Case volume is growing faster than the process around it, so you will be writing and improving the review standards, templates, and escalation paths as much as you follow them. What You'll Own Clinical Case Review Perform clinical case reviews on sepsis alerts: work the encounter record, establish the clinical timeline, determine whether the alert behaved as designed, and produce an internal case review with cited evidence and a recommended next action. Product & Technical Fluency Build and apply working knowledge of how the product generates, suppresses, and delivers flags, including the EHR data that drives it, so your conclusions hold up to both clinical and technical scrutiny. Review the AI-assisted triage and classification our tooling performs, including investigation and complaint classification, ticket creation, and draft acknowledgements, and correct them where the clinical facts don't support the output. Own escalation: route issues to the accountable team in data science, engineering, implementation, or clinical, give them the clinical context they need, and drive tickets through to closure rather than handing them off. Send close-out communications and close resolved tickets. description: About Supabase Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. About the Role We're looking for a SDK Engineer - Python to join our SDK team and own how developers talk to Supabase from Python. You'll work closely with the rest of the SDK team, our Auth, Realtime, Storage, PostgREST, Functions, CLI and Docs teams, and the open-source community, helping us make the Python SDK a library Python developers genuinely enjoy using. Python developers reach Supabase from backend services, data pipelines, notebooks, and a growing number of AI agents and agent frameworks. The Python SDK is how all of them talk to the platform: database queries, auth, storage, realtime and edge functions, in both sync and async flavors. This is a library-authoring role, and the work happens in the open: public repos, public issue trackers, and API decisions whose consequences last for years. If you get satisfaction from a type checker that catches the bug before your users do, from an async client that cleans up after itself, and from an issue tracker that isn't a graveyard, you'll like it here. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions. What You'll Be Responsible For Build and evolve our Python SDK across database, auth, storage, realtime and functions, with both sync and async APIs that feel natural in Python. Start new things. Alongside the maintenance work, find what's missing, make the case for it, and build it. Nobody will hand you the list. Work in the open. Triage inbound issues, review and shepherd outside contributions, keep CI and release automation healthy, and hold a clear, kind line on scope. Own the typing experience. Make the SDK fully typed and checker-friendly, so autocomplete and static analysis stay correct in real codebases. Keep us honest across environments. Multiple Python versions, sync and async frameworks, workers, serverless and notebooks — with dependency ranges that don't fight our users' projects. Test it, don't assume it. Work on realtime. Long-lived websocket connections, reconnection, and subscription and presence semantics. Track the platform. When auth, realtime, storage, postgrest or edge functions ship a change, make sure the SDK reflects it, and that we say so in the changelog. Design in public. Write the RFCs, migration guides, release notes and docs. Treat a breaking change as a deprecation path plus a migration story, not a version bump. Make our SDK legible to AI coding agents, which are now a major consumer of it. You Might Be a Good Fit If You Know modern Python typing deeply. You use generics, protocols, overloads and TypedDict as design tools, run strict type checking, and fix type errors without reaching for Any. Have authored or maintained a published library with a public API and users outside your own company. You know what it costs to change something people depend on. Know the maintainer side of open source. Issue triage at volume, reviewing outside PRs, release automation, changelogs and semver, security reports, and saying no to a feature request without losing the person who asked. Are fluent in asyncio and have opinions on how a library should serve both sync and async callers. Know Python packaging for libraries: pyproject.toml, wheels, modern tooling, version support policy, and why libraries shouldn't pin their dependencies tightly. Test as a habit: unit, type-level and end-to-end against a real stack. Every fix comes with a regression test. Write well. Design docs, changelogs and issue replies are a large part of the output here, much of it public, and we're async by default. Have real autonomy: you find the important work, scope it, ship it, and say what you didn't do. Communicate clearly across both technical and non-technical audiences Have experience in async or globally distributed teams Are energized by solving real-world problems for developers Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and moving quickly Bonus points if you: have run a major-version migration for a public package, know your way around JWT/OAuth, have built integrations for AI agent frameworks, or have generated idiomatic clients from a schema. What We Offer Fully Remote We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world. ESOP Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together. Tech Allowance Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work. Health Benefits Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us. Annual Off-Sites Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year. Flexible Work We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when. Professional Development Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth. About the Team Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love. ~400 team members 60+ countries 20+ languages spoken Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F) 540,000+ community members We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

description: Why Socure? Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day. We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading. About the Job Build the graph that decides who’s real. Every day, Socure’s Identity Graph helps businesses decide whether to trust the person on the other side of a screen. It links billions of signals (names, addresses, devices, emails, phones) into one picture of identity, and it does this in milliseconds. Fraudsters move fast. The graph has to be faster. As a Staff Engineer on this team, you’ll set the technical direction for the platform behind that decision. You’ll own hard problems end to end, work across Engineering, Data Science, Product, and Security, and see your work shape the products that protect millions of people. What You Will Do Shape the graph. Define the schemas, relationships, and ontology that make identity data consistent and extensible. Own entity resolution at scale. Decide how records, people, devices, and addresses connect, and how confident we are, across data that is messy, sparse, and sometimes adversarial. Build for speed and volume. Design batch and real-time pipelines, low-latency APIs, and serving systems that hold up under heavy load. Power fraud intelligence. Ship the production systems behind our ML features, model inference, and graph analytics. Move the numbers. Improve performance, reliability, and cost, and prove it with measurements. Set the direction. Lead architecture decisions, document the tradeoffs, and carry initiatives from first design through production rollout. Raise the bar. Mentor engineers and set the standard for design reviews, testing, CI/CD, and operations. Protect identity data. Build privacy, security, and PII protection into every system from day one. Your toolkit: Java, Scala, or Python. Spark, Kafka, Flink, Airflow, and AWS, including EMR. Graph technologies like Neo4j and Amazon Neptune. What You Will Bring Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, or related field 7+ years building and running distributed systems in the cloud, with at least 2 at Staff or Senior Staff scope, or the equivalent Production scale you can quantify. You can tell us what you built, how big it was, and how much you improved latency, reliability, or cost Deep Spark, Kafka, or Flink experience in both batch and streaming, including debugging them in production Low-latency serving. You have built and tuned APIs where milliseconds matter Graph or entity-resolution experience. You have modeled connected data, matched records across noisy sources, or built an identity graph. Fraud or identity verification is a strong plus Cloud and operations fluency. AWS, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, and real production observability ML data pipelines on Databricks, SageMaker, or similar, plus orchestration with Airflow or equivalent Technical leadership. You have led ambiguous, cross-team work, mentored engineers, and changed the direction of a system through design docs and influence, not authority What This Job is Not It’s not a role for someone who hasn’t owned a system end to end in production, including being on call for it. It’s not feature work on platforms someone else designed. It’s not a defined backlog. You’ll frame ambiguous problems yourself. It’s not a place to treat data privacy as a compliance checkbox. Oversee daily sales support operations, ensuring timely and effective resolution of sales representative inquiries related to quoting, Salesforce processes, commercial policies, and other operational needs. Establish clear escalation paths and SLAs to ensure consistent, high-quality support. If you require a reasonable adjustment due to a disability, or if you prefer a non-automated review of your application, please contact Panopto Talent Attraction. We respect your right to request human intervention; please note that opting for a manual review may impact the standard processing timeline. Data Privacy and Security: Your personal data and recordings are processed securely in compliance with global privacy and employment regulations (including EEOC, GDPR, and other local or regional privacy laws, as applicable). To facilitate our recruitment and evaluation process, limited candidate data may be shared securely with trusted third-party vendors and service providers acting on our behalf. We retain candidate data only as long as necessary to fulfill the recruitment purpose or as required by applicable statutory retention periods. Once this purpose is met, or the retention period expires, your data is securely deleted or anonymized in accordance with our data governance policy. Panopto is dedicated to a fair and equitable hiring process for all candidates. We believe in providing a level playing field where candidates can use modern tools to put their best foot forward, provided those tools support, rather than replace, their authentic voice and expertise. While we encourage the use of AI as a tool for growth and preparation, we require transparency and authenticity to ensure a fair evaluation for all. Acceptable Use: AI-Assisted Preparation: You are encouraged to use Generative AI (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini) as a mock interviewer or coach to refine your speaking points. Research & Knowledge Gathering: Using AI to synthesize industry trends or company background is permitted and viewed as proactive preparation. Career Guidance Tools: Simulation tools that help you practice the STAR method or identify skill gaps are acceptable. Prohibited Use: Live Interview Assistance: The use of real-time AI "teleprompters," live answer-generators, or deepfake audio/video during Panopto recordings or live sessions is strictly prohibited. Plagiarized Work Samples: Any take-home assignments or portfolios must be your original work. While AI can assist in formatting or brainstorming, the core logic and execution must be yours. Panopto has a zero-tolerance policy toward the misrepresentation of job-related skills. Consequences of using prohibited tools may result in my immediate disqualification from the hiring process, the withdrawal of any pending offer, or termination of employment if discovered after hire. Digital Footprint & Professional Links: We may request links to professional profiles (e.g., LinkedIn, GitHub, Behance) to verify career trajectory and industry contributions. Disclosures: Live Validation: Any technical skill demonstrated in an asynchronous Panopto recording is subject to a live, "Human-in-the-Loop" technical assessment or deep-dive discussion. Fraud Detection: Please be aware that we utilize metadata analysis and fraud detection tools to ensure the authenticity of all video submissions. By submitting your application and participating in the recruitment process, you acknowledge and consent to Panopto's use of AI, as well as the acceptable and prohibited uses of AI as a candidate, as described above. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale. description: Why Mozilla? Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We’re a distributed team with expertise in Windows, macOS, and Linux-based operating systems. Our responsibilities include developing fixes and improvements for Firefox related to Windows, macOS, and Linux environments. This might include integration with a new OS feature or fixing an OS-specific user interface bug. Other responsibilities include native crash reporting, OS abstraction layers, sandboxing, hardening, updater, and enterprise DLP support. About the role: As a member of the OS Integration team, you’ll develop fixes, improvements, and new features for Firefox. In many cases work may be cross-platform or have a cross-platform component. This role will include maintenance and development of the installer and updater of Firefox. You’ll contribute to the team through code review and discussion. What you’ll do: Improve the quality of Firefox and other Mozilla products by debugging and fixing software defects, improving the browsing experience for hundreds of millions of users. Contribute to new features and improvements. Break down tasks and work with others to deliver solutions. Collaborate with experienced software engineers. Perform code reviews and provide technical direction. Work with a geographically-distributed development team. Interact with teams throughout the organization. What you’ll bring: 5+ years of overall software engineering experience Strong knowledge of C and C++ Experience with desktop application development on Windows, macOS, or Linux with C++. Knowledge of web technologies such as Javascript and HTML. Knowledge of secure coding practices and memory safety concerns. Strong problem-solving and debugging skills. description: 🌀 The Company Founded in 2022, Filigran is a global cybersecurity company on a mission to empower defense teams to be proactive through open-source solutions that uncover threats and drive action. Filigran stands out in the cybersecurity ecosystem through its open-source, AI-powered and threat-informed approach to Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action. At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative. As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future. 🎯 The Role We're looking for a Staff AppSec / Product Security Engineer to join our Digital Security team, and make security a built-in quality of everything we ship across the XTM platform (OpenCTI, OpenAEV, XTM One, XTM Hub). You'll work closely with the R&D team: the VP, Staff and Principal Engineers, Engineering Managers, Product Owners and the Product Manager. You'll help keep our open source and enterprise products trustworthy for the 6,000+ organizations that defend themselves with them. This is not a solo audit role. As a Staff engineer, you advise the CISO on product security and turn their strategy into day-to-day practice in the product teams. You lead security as a cross-cutting concern, and coach engineers so they own security in their own scope. And of course, you still code: critical security fixes, PR reviews, pair programming and the shared security components that make the secure path the easy one. 💼 Your Responsibilities Leverage AI tools and methodologies to boost productivity and impact Contribute to building AI capabilities into internal workflows Advise the CISO on product security strategy across the XTM platform, and lead its operational implementation in the product teams: turn priorities into concrete actions, and track security technical pains to resolution. Lead threat modeling and security reviews in feature refinements with Product Owners: authentication and RBAC, multi-tenancy, connectors, the GraphQL API, and AI and agent features. Ensure the security quality of the stack through critical PRs, fixes and code reviews, and build shared, secure-by-default components (authorization, secrets, safe outbound calls, input handling). Drive secure SDLC and supply chain tooling in CI (SAST, SCA, secret and container scanning, Renovate, Snyk, SBOMs, signed releases), tuned so teams trust the results. Run product vulnerability management: intake from the open source community, researchers and bug bounty, coordinated disclosure, CVEs and advisories, remediation SLAs, and the product side of security incidents. Mentor engineers and grow security champions through pairing, workshops and continuous feedback. Document security architecture decisions so they stay consistent across teams. 🤝 Who You’ll Work With Reports to: the CISO, as part of the Digital Security team. Key collaborators: the R&D team, including Staff and Principal Engineers and Engineering Managers across the product teams, and Product Owners during refinements, Platform Engineering on infrastructure, compliance (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001:2022, FedRamp) and incidents, and Customer Success on customer security questions and pentest findings. Community: the OpenCTI and OpenAEV open source contributors and the security researchers who report vulnerabilities to us. Mentorship: no direct reports. You'll act as the security technical reference and mentor for engineers across all teams, and grow a network of security champions. 🧬 Profile We’re Looking For Strong interest in AI and its applications in cybersecurity Comfortable working with and leveraging AI-powered tools (LLMs, automation, copilots, etc.) to improve workflows and productivity Master degreee in computer science and or cybersecurity with 8+ years of experience in software engineering and application or product security, including at least 3 years as the security technical reference for a SaaS or enterprise product Comfortable working in a remote, async-first environment Strong engineering and security skills: you write production code fluently in at least two of Python, Node.js, TypeScript, Java or Rust, and you know web and API security in depth (GraphQL, OIDC/SAML, RBAC, multi-tenant isolation, SSRF, injection), CI/CD security tooling, and container and Kubernetes security A track record of influence without authority: you led a cross-team security initiative, coached engineers, and got standards adopted with pragmatism and clear priorities Autonomy, ownership, and team spirit Bonus: AI and LLM security (prompt injection, agent permissions), open source contributions or published CVEs, bug bounty program experience, knowledge of STIX 2.1 / MITRE ATT&CK or hands-on use of OpenCTI or OpenAEV 🌱 Why Join Filigran?
